title: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
summary: A pulldown with a wide overhand grip, for the lats and upper back.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: lat pulldown station (seat and thigh pad).

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for lats (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.6 for upper back (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.4 for traps (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.4 for biceps (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly biceps total.
Library rating 0.3 for rear delts (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly rear delts total.

setup.text: Grip the bar well outside shoulder width and sit with your thighs under the pad.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, driving your elbows down.
Let the bar go up until your arms are straight.

form_cues.cue: Pull the bar to your upper chest
Lean back only slightly. This isn't a row.

mistakes.text: Pulling the bar behind the neck.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less lat-width focus, One side at a time, Narrower grip.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less stretch emphasis, Less lat-width focus, Less stable.
